chapterTitle: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 01 (Unit 10 & 11: Gaseous Exchange & Homeostasis)
subject: biology-10

questions.question: Which structure prevents food and liquids from entering the trachea during swallowing? (FBISE Annual 2024)
questions.explanation: The epiglottis folds down over the glottis during deglutition, preventing aspirated food particles from entering the respiratory tree.

questions.question: What is the primary site of rapid respiratory gas exchange in human lungs?
questions.explanation: Alveoli provide an expansive, moist surface area surrounded by capillary beds where oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse rapidly.

questions.question: During inhalation in humans, which combination of muscle actions occurs?

options.A: Diaphragm relaxes into dome shape and ribs move down
options.B: Diaphragm contracts and flattens, while external intercostal muscles elevate ribs
options.D: Abdominal wall muscles compress thoracic contents

questions.explanation: Inhalation is active: contraction and flattening of the diaphragm combined with contraction of external intercostals expands thoracic volume.

questions.question: The respiratory disorder characterized by permanent destruction of alveolar septa, creating enlarged air spaces and reducing surface area, is: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Emphysema involves irreversible destruction of elastic alveolar walls, leading to trapped air and impaired gas diffusion.

questions.question: The toxic component in tobacco smoke that binds irreversibly with hemoglobin, drastically lowering blood oxygen capacity, is:
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin with an affinity 200 times higher than oxygen, forming stable carboxyhemoglobin.

questions.question: The microscopic structural and functional filtration unit of the human kidney is the: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Each human kidney contains roughly 1 million microscopic nephrons that filter metabolic waste and maintain water-solute balance.

questions.question: In which part of the nephron does hydrostatic pressure-driven ultrafiltration of blood occur? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: High blood pressure inside the glomerulus forces water and small dissolved solutes through capillary walls into Bowman capsule.

questions.question: Which hormone secreted by the posterior pituitary regulates water reabsorption in the collecting ducts of the kidney?
questions.explanation: ADH increases water permeability in collecting ducts, facilitating water retention and producing concentrated urine.

questions.question: Plants adapted to survive in arid, drought-stricken desert environments are classified as: (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Xerophytes possess thick cuticles, sunken stomata, and succulent water-storing tissues to minimize transpirational water loss.

questions.question: The exudation of liquid water droplets through hydathodes along leaf margins under high root pressure is termed:
questions.explanation: Guttation occurs at night or in humid air when root pressure pushes liquid sap out through marginal hydathodes.

questions.question: The non-invasive clinical procedure that breaks kidney stones into passable sand-like gravel using acoustic shock waves is: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) focuses high-energy ultrasonic pulses to pulverize kidney stones into fragments.

questions.question: In hemodialysis, metabolic waste products move across the artificial semipermeable membrane from blood into dialysate primarily by:
questions.explanation: Urea and excess solutes diffuse down their concentration gradients from blood into the constantly flowing dialysate fluid.
